result: Reviewed human entries read 2026-10-21 through rest.uniprot.org. CYP3A4 (P08684), CYP2D6 (P10635), CYP2C9 (P11712), CYP2C19 (P33261), CYP1A2 (P05177) and CYP2E1 (P05181) are cytochrome P450 monooxygenases of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane, CYP2E1 also of the mitochondrial inner membrane; each inserts one atom of molecular oxygen into a substrate and reduces the second to a water molecule, with two electrons provided by NADPH via cytochrome P450 reductase, and each catalyses the hydroxylation of carbon-hydrogen bonds. CYP2D6 is also involved in the oxidative metabolism of drugs such as antiarrhythmics, adrenoceptor antagonists and tricyclic antidepressants; CYP2C19 in that of S-mephenytoin, omeprazole, proguanil, certain barbiturates, diazepam, propranolol, citalopram and imipramine; CYP2E1 in that of xenobiotics (probable). POR (P16435), NADPH-cytochrome P450 reductase, is required for electron transfer from NADP to cytochrome P450 in microsomes. UGT2B7 (P16662), of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane, conjugates lipophilic substrates with glucuronic acid, which increases the water solubility of the metabolite and so its excretion into urine or bile: glucuronate acceptor + UDP-alpha-D-glucuronate = acceptor beta-D-glucuronoside + UDP + H+. SULT1A1 (P50225) uses 3'-phospho-5'-adenylyl sulfate (PAPS) as sulfonate donor for acceptors bearing a hydroxyl or amine group, a phenol + PAPS = an aryl sulfate + adenosine 3',5'-bisphosphate + H+, with broad specificity for small phenolic compounds and sulfate conjugation of xenobiotics including acetaminophen and minoxidil (by similarity); sulfonation raises water solubility and renal excretion of most compounds but can also bioactivate, as with carcinogenic N-hydroxyarylamines. NAT2 (P11245) catalyses the N- or O-acetylation of arylamine and heterocyclic amine substrates, an arylamine + acetyl-CoA = an N-acetylarylamine + CoA, and participates in the detoxification of hydrazine and arylamine drugs while bioactivating several known carcinogens. TPMT (P51580) catalyses the S-methylation of thiopurine drugs such as mercaptopurine and 6-thioguanine with S-adenosyl-L-methionine as methyl donor, and its activity modulates the cytotoxic effects of thiopurine prodrugs; no natural substrate has been identified. SLCO1B1 (Q9Y6L6, OATP1B1), of the basolateral hepatocyte membrane, mediates Na+-independent uptake of organic anions, among them taurocholate, conjugated steroids, eicosanoids, thyroid hormones, bilirubin glucuronides and HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors such as pravastatin and pitavastatin, with hydrogencarbonate the probable counteranion. ABCB1 (P08183, P-glycoprotein), of the apical cell membrane, is an energy-dependent efflux pump responsible for decreased drug accumulation in multidrug-resistant cells, translocates phospholipids and drugs across the membrane, and may contribute to hepatobiliary and renal excretion of etiocholanolone-3-glucuronate. ABCG2 (Q9UNQ0, BCRP), also of the apical cell membrane, is an ATP-dependent transporter of broad substrate specificity that extrudes physiological compounds, dietary toxins and xenobiotics, as well as urate, sulfate conjugates and protoporphyrin IX; it operates at the apical membranes of polarised cells such as hepatocytes and intestinal epithelial cells, where it may contribute to the efflux of conjugated substrates from intestine and liver into the intestinal lumen, and it exports urate in both renal and extrarenal urate excretion.
